content:
Security bug report: request schemas set to boolean `false` are silently ignored.

In JSON Schema, `false` matches nothing, so a route declaring
`schema: { body: false }` should reject every request body. Today Fastify
treats such a schema as if no schema had been declared at all: validation is
skipped and the handler runs. The same happens for `querystring` (including
its documented `query` alias), `params` and `headers`.

Fix it so boolean request schemas are compiled and enforced like any other
schema:

- A `false` schema on any request part (body, querystring or its `query`
  alias, params, headers) rejects every request with 400, and the handler
  never runs. This must also work when that `false` schema is the route's only
  schema.
- A custom `validatorCompiler` receives the literal `false` schema (with the
  right `httpPart`).
- Warning FSTWRN001 (a route declaring an undefined schema) is still emitted
  for schemas that are explicitly `undefined`, and not for `false`.
- A `null` schema is invalid: `fastify.ready()` must fail with
  `FST_ERR_SCH_VALIDATION_BUILD` instead of accepting requests.
- Declaring both `query` and `querystring` on one route must still throw.

Work within this local repository and the context you have been given. Do not
look up this project or its history online.

Verify your work before you finish: add or update automated tests that cover
the change, run them together with the existing tests for the code you touched,
and make sure they pass.

This repository includes an agent context pack generated by Razor. Before you

Boolean `false` request schemas are now compiled and enforced like any other schema. The full unit suite passes (2327 pass, 3 skipped, 0 fail) and eslint is clean.

I did not run `scripts/check.sh` as a whole, only `eslint` and `npm run unit`, so `npm run lint` and `npm run test:types` are unchecked.

The cause was truthiness checks on `body`, `querystring`/`query`, `params` and `headers`: `false` was treated the same as "not declared". The checks now compare against `undefined`.

- **`lib/validation.js`:** `false` and `null` schemas are passed to the compiler instead of being skipped. FSTWRN001 is still emitted only for an explicit `undefined`.
- **`lib/schemas.js`:** the `query` alias is applied when `query !== undefined`, so `query: false` works. The duplicate check on `querystring` now uses `!== undefined`, so declaring both still throws `FST_ERR_SCH_DUPLICATE`.
- **`lib/route.js`:** `hasValidationSchema` uses `!== undefined`, so a route whose only schema is `false` still sets up the validator.
- **`null`:** a `null` schema makes `fastify.ready()` fail with `FST_ERR_SCH_VALIDATION_BUILD`.
- **Tests:** new `test/schema-false.test.js` (17 tests) covers body, querystring, `query`, params and headers for the 400 rejection, the literal `false` and `httpPart` seen by a custom compiler, and `null` failing `ready()`. It also covers the FSTWRN001 behaviour and the duplicate-declaration error.

A `GET` route also registers `HEAD`, so a custom compiler is called twice per part; the tests allow for that.
